jobs.title: Data Consultant - Logistics
jobs.snippet: Overview We are seeking a mid-level Data Consultant to design, implement, and maintain robust data models and data exchange solutions supporting manufacturing and plant logistics operations. In this role, you will work hands-on with business and functional teams to translate operational supply chain workflows into logical, physical, and dimensional models, while developing the underlying Oracle PL/SQL mechanisms and data integration pipelines.   Roles & Responsibilities : Data Consultant (Data Modeling & Logistics Solutions) Data Modeling & Architecture: Design, implement, and maintain logical and physical data models, dimensional schemas (star/snowflake), and data vault structures using Oracle Data Modeler or equivalent tools. Implementation Projects: Actively contribute to and execute end-to-end data modeling and engineering implementation and rollout lifecycles for business-critical operational applications. Database Programming & Customization: Develop and maintain stored procedures, packages, functions, and triggers in Oracle PL/SQL tailored to business requirements and operational logic. Data Integration & Exchange: Design and implement robust data interface and delta-capture mechanisms, ETL routines, and automated file exchange processes (SFTP/FTP) between ERP, WMS/MES, and downstream data repositories. Performance Tuning & Debugging: Perform query optimization, indexing strategies, debugging, and execution-plan tuning to ensure high performance and data accuracy.

jobs.title: Software Development Engineer - Tejas
jobs.snippet: Enterprises want agents that can do real work on their own data. That data sits across documents, databases and business systems that were never built for agents to read, and today's agents forget most of what they learn once a session ends. Our team builds Sarvam's context engine to solve both problems. The knowledge side brings an enterprise's data together so agents can search it, navigate it and cite where an answer came from. jobs.title: ASIC Verification Engineer
jobs.snippet: We are looking for a Hardware and Software Developer. The role is multifaceted - SoCV testbench Infrastructure, Bare-metal boot, Silicon Bringup Tools and CPU/SOC/GPU test frameworks. It involves a detailed understanding of the nVidia CPU, GPU, SOC system and boot architectures. The tools and technologies are complex and involve code that coordinates many IPs in the overall SOC. A key part of NVIDIA's strength is our development tools and environments that enable our incredible pace of delivering new technology to the market. We are looking for a creative and hardworking engineer who is passionate about joining a dynamic & agile SoCV/Emulation Infrastructure and test-frameworks team. What you will be doing: The work includes building tools, infrastructure, and test frameworks used in RTL-simulations, c-simulations, Emulation, FPGA, and on Silicon. You will understand Tegra system architecture, with a focus on all IPs in the SOC that are involved in boot and security features. The tools that you build give Design and Verification teams the ability to access registers/memory/DMA engines and other features in their unit. The tools also enable test re-use across multiple platforms (RTL, models, Emulation, and Silicon). The gamut of tools is wide and you also develop features used for Silicon bring up (example: FUSE, ATE, Security, Flash/DMA, Board I2Cs, USB debug devices among others). We strive for the highest quality of test frameworks and tools that we deliver from this team.

jobs.title: Agent Engineer
jobs.snippet: The distance between an AI system that works and one that millions of people rely on every day is where the real engineering lives. Crossing it is what Agent Engineers at Sarvam do. The agents you build go into live operation at India's largest banks, insurers, NBFCs and government departments, and at some of the country's fastest-growing companies, handling millions of real interactions, measured against outcomes the customer wants to drive. The hard part is not the first version. It is everything after: mapping the full space of what an agent has to handle so the scenarios that matter are covered by design rather than discovered in production, engineering for the failure modes instead of the happy path, and building the evals and instrumentation that make quality measurable, so drift surfaces in the data rather than in a customer escalation. We treat agents as code. Not prompts someone tweaks in a console, but engineered artifacts: versioned, reviewed, and held to a regression suite, where you can reason about what a change will do and roll it back if you are wrong. Anyone who has watched an AI system quietly decay because nobody could tell which change broke it understands why this matters. And then doing it again for the next customer, faster, because you built the first one to be repeatable.
